subject: Rapid Acceptance MAP: 3-week evaluation blueprint and ops cadence
messages:
From: Beth Any <beth.any@orionhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, May 20, 2028 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Eval timing and next steps

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. The team liked the latency and the cust-data isolation options you showed. We have an internal goal to validate the integration and basic PII handling within three weeks so procurement can move to budget approval.

Can you share a short, prescriptive MAP we can follow? Ideally it should call out: who owns infra verification, a minimal success checklist, stakeholder reviews, and a proposed weekly ops cadence. Also we’ll need a simple deliverable list so our security folks can tick boxes.

Beth
Beth Any
Director, Platform Partnerships
Orion Health

--

(Attachment: initial-eval-requests.xlsx)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Beth Any <beth.any@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, May 21, 2028 at 10:05 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Rapid Acceptance MAP: draft + shared GDoc

Thanks Beth — great to connect. Attached is a fast MAP we use for 3-week pilots (document + minimal QA checklist). I’ve also created a collaborative Google Doc so we can draft against your security asks and lock owners. Link below.

Top-level plan highlights (TL;DR):
- Week 0 (days 0–3): Access + baseline tests — Orion provides a test dataset slice; Redwood provisions a private sandbox and baseline perf run. Owner: Orion (data), Redwood infra (sandbox).
- Week 1 (days 4–10): Integration + core validation — API wiring, auth checks, basic throughput. Owner: Engineering (Redwood) + Orion SRE. Deliverable: integration runbook + sample output.
- Week 2 (days 11–17): Security & PII checks, acceptance tests — red-teaming prompts, retention confirmation, audit log sampling. Owner: Security teams. Deliverable: SOC-style checklist + failing cases.
- Week 3 (days 18–21): Stakeholder review & decision window — product demo, ops handoff, procurement signoff.

I’ve assigned section owners inside the GDoc comments. Marissa — can you draft the acceptance criteria table and include token/cost targets? Jasmine — can you pull the list of infra validation steps (networking, KMS key check, egress rules) and paste into Week 0/1.

GDoc (edit): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2b3C4-redwood-rapid-map
Attachments: redwood-rapid-acceptance-map-v1.docx (template), orion-requested-eval-metrics.xlsx (from Beth)

Next steps:
1) Beth — can you confirm who from Orion will be the SRE and security reviewers (name + email)?
2) Marissa/Jasmine — 48hr to drop first pass into the GDoc.
3) I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff on Friday to align owners if that works.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-rapid-acceptance-map-v1.docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, May 22, 2028 at 08:34 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Rapid Acceptance MAP: draft + shared GDoc

Diego — putting my notes here after a quick pass through the template. I left inline comments in the GDoc for decision gates and added a proposed acceptance table. Key asks I added:
- Define "minimal viable correctness" (sample pass rate on 500 synthetic records)
- Token cost cap for Week 1 burst tests (we should give Orion a hard ceiling)
- Explicit rollback criteria (if avg latency > 2x baseline or error rate > 1.5%)

I uploaded a starter sheet with the acceptance table: redwood-acceptance-table-week0-3.csv (in GDoc attachments). Jasmine — can you confirm the KMS validation steps and whether we need an HSM checklist for Orion?

I’ll take ownership of the acceptance matrix and the final walkthrough slides for Week 3 demo. Dropping a few items into the GDoc now.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
